adoption_spec.rationale: Lost-in-the-middle (2307.03172, TACL 2024, most-replicated item): models retrieve best at start/end of context, degrade mid-context. On long handoff chains, mid-chain state gets buried. Put goal+constraints+prior-decisions at the END of each hop's prompt. LangGraph Command + OpenAI handoff() typed metadata are the in-stack mechanisms to carry state explicitly (vs implicit transcript accumulation).
adoption_spec.constraint_fit: federation is ALREADY LangGraph — adopt Command handoff with state-carrying. Complements 15-min repomap (which refreshes CODE structure, not TASK state).

adoption_spec.title: Learned/generated per-task topology (G-Designer / GPTSwarm) — SPIKE, do not adopt yet
adoption_spec.rationale: G-Designer (2410.11782): VGAE generates per-query topology, -92.24% tokens on HumanEval, 0.3% adversarial drop vs 6-11% static. GPTSwarm (2402.16823): learns edges via REINFORCE, HumanEval +12pp, GAIA +90% rel, auto-prunes bad agents. HALO (2505.13516): 3-tier recursive hierarchy, MATH +22pp vs ADAS. ADaPT (2311.05772): failure-triggered recursion, +33% TextCraft. HIGH impact but require RL training / graph models = heavy, and benefit is largest at agent counts we don't run (Google 3-4 ceiling). DEFER: the A1 decomposability gate captures ~80% of the win (don't-fan-out-when-sequential) at effort 2 vs 5.
adoption_spec.constraint_fit: Most are research-grade, need local training. Re-evaluate only if fleet grows past current 2-7 bound (which Google scaling says NOT to do).

adoption_spec.title: Optimistic concurrency (version-vector CAS) for shared scratchpad — not a new Redis lease
adoption_spec.target: shared-artifact writes (events_outbox / scratchpad) — NOT the L2 hot-zone lease
adoption_spec.rationale: At 2-7 agents, OCC (version/compare-and-set + retry) beats pessimistic locking because conflicts are rare and retries cheap. Our L2 Redis lease is correct for HOT-ZONE files (plist/migrations) but over-engineered for a shared scratchpad — version-vector CAS on existing Postgres events_outbox suffices. Keep L2 lease for hot-zones (sunk cost, kill-switch), use OCC for scratchpad if/when one is added.
adoption_spec.constraint_fit: Postgres already present; no new infra. Narrow scope — does NOT replace L2.

adoption_spec.title: REJECT A2A protocol + MCP-as-peer-coordination for our scale
adoption_spec.rationale: A2A (v1.0.0, Linux Foundation, 150+ orgs) standardizes CROSS-ORGANIZATIONAL agent interop (Agent Card discovery, JSON-RPC/gRPC transports, webhook push). Built for heterogeneous agents across org/vendor boundaries — over-engineered for 2-7 LOCAL same-codebase Claude sessions under Law 6 sovereignty. MCP sampling/elicitation is client-side, routed through host — NOT symmetric P2P; using it as agent-coordination creates hidden host routing (MAST FC1). Our CLI-subprocess + Postgres EventBus is the right local layer.
adoption_spec.constraint_fit: Reject preserves Law 6 (no external protocol surface). Revisit only if Bali Zero ever federates with external agent vendors.

adoption_spec.title: REJECT Kafka event-backbone + full blackboard infra; borrow self-selection IDEA only
adoption_spec.rationale: Confluent (vendor, second-hand): Kafka backbone supports 4 patterns but infra cost only pays off ABOVE small agent counts. We already have Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY + events_outbox (EventBus shipped). Blackboard self-selection (2510.01285: +13-57% rel success) is a GOOD idea — removes the brittle requirement that CLASSIFY know every lane's capability — but adopt the PRINCIPLE (lanes self-declare capability, graceful add/remove) not the Kafka infra. Captured partly by A1+A3.
adoption_spec.constraint_fit: No new infra (Law 6). The self-selection principle informs A1's classifier design.
